Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have alignment before the architecture deep-dive: 

Call highlights
- Goal: user-facing assistant at Clearline.com with 99.9% availability and p95 latency <= 550ms for text responses (non-streaming) under steady-state traffic.
- Expected steady QPS: 250 requests/sec across NA region, peak bursts ~700 QPS for marketing events.
- Streaming: ~18% of sessions will use streaming audio->text->response with median output token length ~120 tokens, worst-case 450 tokens.
- Accuracy guardrail: priority is correctness on domain-specific retrieval hits; fallback to smaller model must maintain acceptable fidelity for top-1 answers.

Initial qualification asks (what we need from you)
1) Representative load trace / 24-72h sample (timestamps + qps) — helps sizing for batching/capacity.
2) Typical and worst-case token counts for requests and responses (we need percentiles: p50/p95/p99).
3) Any hard SLA requirements for streaming sessions (e.g., first-byte latency).
4) Security/compliance constraints we should know up-front (data residency, retention windows).

Attachments: I attached the quick sample format we usually accept (clearline-metrics-sample.csv) — if you can fill/confirm, our SEs will run a sizing pass and deliver a 1-page ops matrix (latency buckets, concurrency, cost levers).

Next steps
- You: send the sample traces + token percentiles and call out any legal/KMS constraints.
- We: SE pass + rough cost delta comparing 1) conservative (no quantization, dedicated capacity) and 2) cost-optimized path (intelligent batching, 8-bit quantization, model variants). Aim to deliver by Fri 9/17.
- Schedule: propose a 60-min architecture deep-dive next week once we have traces.

Thanks — putting Ben and Marissa on the thread to start the sizing.

Regards,

Logan — quick SE pass based on the trace Samantha sent. Notes, trade-offs, and a short cost-path matrix we can present to Clearline during the deep-dive: 

Quick observations
- p95 response 210 tokens with p99 420 means KV cache hit is huge opportunity for cost reduction if they have repeat prompts.
- Streaming first-byte <120ms is tight but achievable with prefix caching + continuous batching tuned for streaming pipelines.

Cost / performance levers (prioritized)
1) Continuous batching + adaptive batch sizing
   - Benefit: increases GPU utilization across steady QPS; reduces token cost by ~25–40% depending on sequence length; minimal impact on p50 latency when tuned.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (user history, common retrievals)
   - Benefit: reduces compute for cached prefixes; best-case p95 improvement and cost reduction for repeat flows.
3) Quantization profiles (8-bit LLMs for non-critical routes; 4-bit via restricted variants for bulk throughput)
   - Benefit: 30–60% cost reduction vs fp16; need to validate accuracy drift for their domain retrievals.
4) Model routing (high-fidelity model for retrieval hits; smaller model fallback for generic chit-chat)
   - Benefit: keeps accuracy where it matters, lowers average cost.

Preliminary sizing ask
- Can we get a 72h trace for us-west and eu-west traffic split? Marissa will run a quick runbook for cost-estimate scenarios and produce a two-page ops matrix (latency buckets, concurrency targets, estimated monthly spend across three tiers).

Draft deliverables for 9/17 (internal)
- Ops matrix v0 (Marissa) + cost-estimates-v1.xlsx (attached)
- Proposed MAPP skeleton for Clearline (I'll draft)

Quoted for context: "First-byte requirement: prefer <120ms for first token" (from Samantha).
